1. **Keep a consistent sleep schedule.** Go to bed and wake up at the same time every day, even on weekends. This trains your circadian rhythm so your body knows when to wind down.

2. **Make your bedroom cool, dark, and quiet.** Aim for around 65–68 °F (18–20 °C), use blackout curtains or a sleep mask, and eliminate noise with earplugs or a fan. A restful environment lowers your core body temperature and reduces the micro-arousals that fragment sleep.
